definition: The season around All Hallows’ Eve, All Saints’ Day, and All Souls’ Day; traditionally, October 31 through November 2.
etymology: English joined hallow, once meaning a saint or holy person and descended from Old English hālga, to tide, an old word for a stretch of time or season. Thus the saints were given their own little season.
usage: By late October, lanterns in the windows announce the approach of Hallowtide.
